sections.content: How many people are "managers and proprietors in other services (other)"?

174,900 people

were counted on the census as "managers and proprietors in other services (other)" in England and Wales in March 2021.
People who do this type of work perform a variety of managerial tasks in other service industries not elsewhere classified.

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 50 to 54 years. Of the whole working population 11.7% were aged 50 to 54 years. For people working as "managers and proprietors in other services (other)", 14.2% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "managers and proprietors in other services (other)" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "managers and proprietors in other services (other)" included:

  • travel agency managers and proprietors
  • managers in transport and distribution
  • residential, day and domiciliary care managers and proprietors

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "managers and proprietors in other services (other)" there were more men than women (58.5% compared with 41.5%).

This means "managers and proprietors in other services (other)" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "other managers and proprietors".

Men made up 58.5% and women made up 41.5% of "managers and proprietors in other services (other)"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "managers and proprietors in other services (other)" included:

  • environment professionals
  • specialist medical practitioners
  • data analysts

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "managers and proprietors in other services (other)" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "managers and proprietors in other services (other)" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "managers and proprietors in other services (other)", 9.1% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (71.1% compared with 28.9%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (58.9%) than self-employed (41.1%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Buckinghamshire, this is in the same region of the South East.
